title: Understanding temperature tuning in energy-based models
abstract: arXiv:2512.09152v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Generative models of complex systems often require post hoc parameter adjustments to produce useful outputs. For example, energy-based models for protein design are sampled at an artificially low "temperature" to generate novel, functional sequences. This temperature tuning is a common yet poorly understood heuristic used across machine learning contexts to control the trade-off between generative fidelity and diversity. Here, we develop an interpretable, physically motivated framework to explain this phenomenon. We demonstrate that in systems with a large "energy gap" separating a small fraction of meaningful states from a vast space of unrealistic states, learning from sparse data causes models to systematically overestimate high-energy state probabilities, a bias that lowering the sampling temperature corrects. translated_title: 理解基于能量的模型中的温度调节
translated_abstract: 复杂系统的生成模型通常需要事后参数调整才能产生有用的输出。例如，用于蛋白质设计的基于能量的模型会在人为调低的“温度”下进行采样，以生成新颖且具有功能性的序列。这种温度调节是机器学习领域中一种常见但尚未被充分理解的启发式方法，用于控制生成保真度与多样性之间的权衡。在此，我们开发了一个可解释的、具有物理动机的框架来解释这一现象。我们证明，在存在较大“能隙”的系统中——该能隙将一小部分有意义的状态与 vast 的不现实状态空间分隔开——从稀疏数据中学习会导致模型系统性地高估高能态的概率，而降低采样温度可以纠正这一偏差。更广泛地，我们刻画了最优采样温度如何依赖于数据规模与（摘要原文在此处截断）之间的相互作用。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个可解释的物理框架，解释了在能量基模型中降低采样温度为何能纠正稀疏数据导致的对高能态概率的系统性高估，从而有效调控生成保真度与多样性之间的权衡。
en_tdlr: This paper develops an interpretable, physically motivated framework showing that lowering the sampling temperature in energy-based models corrects a systematic overestimation of high-energy state probabilities caused by sparse data learning, thereby controlling the fidelity-diversity trade-off.
